From Placement to Belonging:
Rethinking Inclusion

A multimodal reflection on disability, access, relationships, and inclusive design.

Shenkaiyi Rong

Page 1 — My Initial Position

At the beginning of the semester, I had a simplified understanding of inclusive education. I thought inclusion mostly meant placing students in the same classroom.

I also associated disability mainly with visible, physical conditions. At that point, my thinking was narrow and mostly focused on physical presence.

My first idea was: inclusion = placement

Page 2 — How My Thinking Developed

This project shows that my thinking changed in three main ways over the semester.

Placement → Access

LRE helped me understand that being present is not the same as being included.

Visible → Invisible

I learned that disability includes invisible conditions, such as ADHD and learning disabilities.

Support → Design

UDL and inclusive pedagogy pushed me to think about designing access from the beginning.

My thinking moved from “where students are” to “how students belong”

Page 3 — Reading Connections

My learning journey connects directly to course readings and course content.

LRE

Changed my thinking from physical placement to meaningful access and participation.

UDL

Moved me from reactive accommodation to proactive design for different learners.

Be the Architect

Helped me understand inclusion as relationship-building and classroom community design.

These also connect to participation structures and inclusive pedagogy, because participation does not happen automatically; it has to be intentionally facilitated.

Page 4 — Corrected Activity Design

After receiving feedback, I realized I needed to revise my earlier approach. Instead of relying on a token-based activity, I shifted toward a relationship-based structured dialogue that better aligns with the course emphasis on participation, relationships, and inclusive design.

Correction

I learned that participation structures should not only be engaging; they also need to align with course goals.

Revision

I redesigned the activity to emphasize listening, representing another person’s perspective, and making voice visible.

Revision became part of my learning

Page 5 — Two Integrated Modalities

Website: This mode shows my analytical development. It organizes my ideas step by step across the semester.

Hand-drawn poster: This mode shows personal reflection. The sketch style lets me express revision, uncertainty, and emotional meaning.

Together, these modes communicate the same learning journey in different but connected ways.

Page 6 — How the Modalities Shaped My Expression

The website helped me express sequence, structure, and analysis. It made it easier to show how my thinking changed over time.

The hand-drawn poster helped me express reflection in a less formal and more personal way. It let me show that my understanding is still developing, rather than fixed.

Because of that, the two modalities do not repeat each other. They express different dimensions of the same reflection.

Page 7 — Inclusive Design and Pedagogy

This project helped me connect more deeply to course ideas about inclusive design because I had to think about how a viewer could enter my reflection in different ways.

The process also deepened my understanding of inclusive pedagogy. I used to think it was mainly about support and good intentions. Now I understand that it is also about structure, access, participation, and design.

Inclusive pedagogy is something I had to practice,
not just define.

Page 8 — Final Reflection

At the beginning of the semester, I thought inclusion was mostly about placement. Now I understand it as access, participation, relationship, equity, and belonging.

This shift happened through readings, discussions, correction, and reflection.

Inclusion is not about being there.
It is about being heard.
